title: Advance Economic Indicators Report (advance goods trade, retail & wholesale inventories, Sep 2026 data)
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html lists 'Advance Economic Indicators Report (International Trade, Retail, & Wholesale) | October 28, 2026 | 8:30 AM | September 2026' (fetched direct 2026-09-05). Primary-sourced, but filed estimate per the event-research lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep — and the series carries its own precedent for non-publication: the same Census page still shows 'Suspended' against the January and February 2026 reference months. Checked 2026-09-05
notes: IT IS THE FINAL Q3 NOWCAST, not merely the last input to it: the Atlanta Fed's own GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx (fetched direct 2026-09-05) schedules the 2026-10-28 08:30 posting as 'Final nowcast of 2026:Q3 GDP growth: Advance Economic Indicators', and the AEIR has held that slot in 26 of 49 quarters and all seven most recent. The initial research (2026-09-05) also measured the leverage the note below asserted from one observation: across 1,871 GDPNow model vintages (2014-05-01 to 2026-07-28), AEIR-driven vintages carry median composition churn of 0.584pp against 0.048pp for every other vintage (12.2x) and median |change in net exports| of 0.265pp against 0.002pp (132x), out-churning even the days GDP itself prints - while moving the headline far less (churn-to-headline ratio 1.47 vs 0.449). Still not tradeable, and the ledger closes that question on measurement rather than on symbols: [] alone - across 21 FOMC decision days the 09:30-12:00 window makes 44.8% (SPY) of the session's range against 80.1% on ordinary sessions. Original note follows. The last hard-data input the GDP nowcast gets before gdp-q3-2026-advance-2026-10-29, landing 08:30 the morning of the FOMC decision and 24 hours before the print itself. It earns a row because it was MEASURED to be the largest single-day mover of the Q3 2026 nowcast's composition: the July-data edition on 2026-08-27 moved GDPNow's equipment contribution 0.48 -> 1.06pp, net exports -0.14 -> -1.31pp and inventories 1.71 -> 2.10pp in one release (headline 4.61 -> 4.40%), per the Atlanta Fed's own GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx fetched 2026-09-05. Those are precisely the two lowest-quality lines that the advance GDP estimate's headline turns on, so this report front-runs the composition question 10-29 is read for. It also carries the advance goods-trade balance that the AI-hardware import surge runs through - the same hardware that adds to equipment investment and subtracts from net exports. Not a tradeable print on its own (symbols: [], no house playbook is macro-keyed); tracked as the corridor's composition tell. Discovered during the gdp-q3-2026-advance-2026-10-29 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-05).
